attribution.note: Marcus endorses the assessment that scaling has not solved the referenced problems; the contrary expectation is attributed to others.

semantics.note: The proposition preserves the retrospective assessment and its emphasis on substantial remaining limitations. It does not claim that scaling can never solve them.

contract.note: Reading the statement as substantial practical limitations persisting through publication is ordinary and fair. The contract appropriately permits improvements and requires more than isolated errors.

evidence.note: The November 2025 benchmark reports recurring GPT-5 hallucinations on challenging summarization tasks. It supports substantial remaining failures in this domain, but neither cross-domain conclusions nor deterioration over time.

OpenAI's company disclosure acknowledges persistent hallucinations while reporting significant improvement. It supports persistence, but does not independently establish how far models remain from dependable performance.

reviews.rationale: The packet establishes recurring hallucinations near publication and substantial earlier physical and social-reasoning failures. It does not establish whether substantial limitations persisted across the referenced areas in contemporary models through publication. Reported improvements and intervention gains also limit inference. The full observation is neither established nor contradicted.
